A parallel OptimusKG-style KG path for who-iris: design and integration options

Status: exploration and design only. This document adds no code, no process files and no beans. It sets out the integration options, a recommendation, and the questions the owner needs to answer before the work items are opened. The existing L1 → KG ingestion is left exactly as it is: the new path runs beside it and never writes the files it writes.

The owner's request, 2026-11-17 (relayed, lightly edited for typos):

need to update who-iris KG to include a new parallel KG process/tooling/skill set. The current L1 → KG ingestion should remain. We have a new one that makes use of a tool 'redacto'. It will adapt https://optimuskg.ai/ . Explore integration paths and document processes. Where outputs are related, we need to align schemas to DAK/WHO schemas. When schema aligned, then need adjudication to compare outputs of different tools. The ingestion process for the Optimus-like KG extract should pull from the nightly who-iris CDN feed to process new materials. As part of the new L1 guideline development process, the editor should describe the articles / evidence / what comprises a guideline of interest for that L1 document. This should be used to develop queries against IRIS DSpace / Dublin Core, as well as provide guidance for agentic review of a library KG (who-iris or external).

1. Findings that shape the design

Three findings change the request as it was written. Each one is stated first because the rest of the design depends on it.

  1. OptimusKG does not extract a graph from documents. It is a reproducible build that merges about 65 structured and semi-structured biomedical databases, such as Open Targets, DrugBank, CTD and Reactome, into one property graph. It has no chunking, no entity or relation extraction from text, and no LLM in the build; an LLM (PaperQA3) appears only in its evaluation. Its code is at mims-harvard/optimuskg and the lab announced it in April 2026. So "adapt OptimusKG" for WHO IRIS PDFs can only mean adopting its architecture, schema shape and provenance model, with a text-extraction front end that OptimusKG does not have. Section 3 lists what carries over.
  2. "redacto" could not be identified. A code search of the litlfred organisation found only a local class Redactor that scrubs e-mail addresses in litlfred/ihris. Searches of issues in litlfred and WorldHealthOrganization found nothing. Several unrelated public repositories have the name; the closest is FredHutch/RedactO, which OCRs PDFs and redacts them. Nothing links any of them to OptimusKG. This design does not guess what redacto does. It leaves a slot for it, Tool B, and section 12 asks the owner for the repository or package. The slot is shaped to accept either an extractor (text → candidate nodes and edges) or a pre-extraction redaction step (PDF → PDF or text with personal data removed). Section 4 shows how each reading changes the plan.
  3. The nightly CDN feed is designed and coded, but it is not consumable yet. processes/iris-cdn-nightly.bpmn and scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts nightly produce a signed BagIt release in a git repository on Cloudflare Artifacts, with bytes in R2. Deployment still has open items (iris-cdn-deployment.md §Still open). The new path should depend on the feed's contract, the verified release and its payload manifest, and not on its run time. Then it can be built and tested against a local release before the feed is live.

A fourth point is a constraint rather than a finding. The gap is the point (AGENTS.md). The nightly feed reports every IRIS change, and IRIS has 273,559 items. The new path must not turn the feed into a bulk import. It processes an item only when an L1 editor's scope of interest (section 8) selects it, and only after the materialisation gates in materialize-remote pass.

2. The existing L1 → KG ingestion, which stays

The current path is folio-assistant-core's library-ingestion chain. smart-base skills then write the L1 knowledge graph from what it derives. Nothing in this design edits these processes or the files they own.

step process (folio-assistant-core processes/library/) what it writes under library/<slug>/
extract structure ingest-extract-structure.bpmn sections/*.md, structure.json, candidates.json, OCR pages
derive content ingest-derive-content.bpmn images.json, vector-*.json, footnotes.json, tabular CSVW
build the L1 KG ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn dublin-core.jsonld, manifest.jsonld, assets, glossary candidates, references/
completeness gate ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn the check:l1-complete verdict. Its round-trip and Task_FlagDrift adjudication are the pattern section 7 reuses
publish statements publish-extracted-statements.bpmn statement pages with source links
L1 KG (smart-base) skill smart-base/extract-smart-kg-l1 smart-kg-l1.json, context http://smart.who.int/kg/l1.context.jsonld: nodes publication, publication-section, recommendation; edges are Statements (contains), each node with derivation and evidence{location, quote}
L1 library KG (smart-base) skill smart-base/dak-l1-library smart-kg-l1-library.jsonld, ontology 3.0: library-node, publication-section, publication-element; edges contains, specializationOf

Today three library entries carry smart-kg-l1-library.jsonld and two carry smart-kg-l1.json. The existing path is section-structural and recommendation-centred: it knows where a statement is in a publication and that the statement is a recommendation. It does not know which disease, drug or exposure the statement is about. That missing layer is what an OptimusKG-style typed entity graph would add, which is why the two outputs are related but not redundant, and why aligning them is worth the effort.

3. OptimusKG: what is worth adapting

Read from the repository at commit 4fb3529 (2026-09-21), its docs site source (docs/content/docs/), and the PyPI client optimuskg 1.0.0 (MIT, Python ≥ 3.12). The client describes the graph as integrating 65 resources grounded with 18 ontologies and vocabularies, with 190,531 nodes in 10 entity types and 21,813,816 edges in 26 relation types. The repository README gives slightly different counts (192,813 nodes, 27 edge labels), so the figures depend on the release. The paper is cited as Vittor et al., "OptimusKG: Unifying biomedical knowledge in a modern multimodal graph", Nature Scientific Data, 2026. optimuskg.ai and arXiv could not be fetched from this session, so the paper's evaluation figures are not quoted here.

aspect OptimusKG adopt for the WHO path?
layers Kedro "medallion": landing → bronze → silver → gold, pure-function nodes in DAG pipelines, a dataset catalog that is the single source of truth for each schema Yes, the shape. landing = verified CDN bytes; bronze = Tool B's raw output; silver = grounded and normalised; gold = aligned to the WHO crosswalk, ready to adjudicate
determinism version-pinned providers, checksum and quality-check hooks, reproducible runs Yes. It matches the CDN's no-churn rule: same input, same bytes
grounding BioCypher + Biolink Model; MONDO, DO, HPO, GO, Orphanet, UBERON; UMLS CUIs kept as properties; CURIE ids Partly. Keep the BioCypher schema-config approach. Ground to WHO vocabularies first (ICD-11, ATC/INN, MeSH as IRIS already carries it, the WHO glossary), with Biolink and MONDO as skos:closeMatch bridges
node types 10: Gene, Drug, Disease, Phenotype, Anatomy, Pathway, Biological Process, Cellular Component, Molecular Function, Exposure Subset. Drug, Disease, Phenotype, Exposure and Anatomy matter for WHO guidance. The molecular types are out of scope unless a scope of interest asks for them
edge shape from, to, label, relation, undirected, properties; at most one edge per (from, to, label) Yes, plus a mandatory evidence locator (section 6)
provenance sources{direct[], indirect[]} on every node and edge; evidence_score/count/index on associations Yes, with direct = the IRIS handle + section + page + quote
conflict model relation_assertions keeps every {source, relation}; relation_conflict flags mutually exclusive ones (339 drug–disease pairs are both INDICATION and CONTRAINDICATION) Yes. This is the seed of the adjudication input. It records disagreement inside one tool; section 7 extends it to disagreement between tools
outputs Parquet gold layer (nodes/*.parquet, edges/*.parquet) on Harvard Dataverse; Neo4j export; the PyPI client optimuskg downloads and caches gold files (get_file, load_parquet, load_graph(lcc=True), load_networkx), pinned to a release by OPTIMUSKG_DOI; MCP bundle on DuckDB; no RDF Parquet as the working form, then projected to N-Quads so the existing Oxigraph partitions (iris-oxigraph) can query both graphs side by side
evaluation PaperQA3 checks sampled edges (100 per node type by centrality, true and false neighbours, a power analysis at α = 0.05) Yes, as the sampling plan for the agentic adjudication in section 7
licence code MIT (© 2025 Zitnik Lab); data keeps each source's licence, some academic or non-commercial only; distributed on Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/IYNGEV Adapting the code patterns is clear under MIT. Importing the OptimusKG data as an external library KG is a separate question, gated by copyright and restrictions (section 12)

4. Integration options and the recommendation

All four options keep the existing path untouched, and all four consume the same CDN contract. They differ in where Tool B runs and where its output lives.

option how for against
A Sibling pipeline in who-iris IRIS-specific scripts in scripts/optimus/; outputs under a new declared directory, e.g. kg-optimus/<slug>/{bronze,silver,gold}/ One repository, same CI, same mounts who-iris is separation: content and tolerates IRIS-specific code only with a QA warning. A Kedro/Python extractor is far more than "a small number of tools" (owner, 2026-10-01)
B A step inside ingest-build-l1-kg a new task after Task_Link No new process Rejected. It is not parallel: it changes the process the owner said must remain, and it couples Tool B's failures to L1 completeness
C External extractor, referenced KG Tool B and the medallion pipeline run in their own repository or service, pinned by version. who-iris holds only orchestration, the crosswalk and adjudication records, and references the gold output by digest Clean split: code where code belongs; the gold output is a remote KG in the materialisation sense, so its subgraph metadata sits under library/<source>/ Two release trains to pin and keep in step
D Import OptimusKG's own graph as an external library KG subscribe to one Dataverse release as a remote KG, read through the optimuskg client pinned by OPTIMUSKG_DOI; only the node and edge files a scope needs (e.g. nodes/drug.parquet, nodes/disease.parquet and the DRG–DIS edges) are fetched, and their metadata is held under library/optimuskg/; no extraction Gives drug–disease grounding at once Biomedical-database facts, not WHO guidance. Licences vary per source. Useful only as a grounding and comparison reference for section 8's agentic review, never as Tool B

Recommendation: C for the extractor runtime, with A's thin orchestration layer in who-iris. The parts are placed in section 10.

  • who-iris holds the IRIS-specific feed consumer, the processes, the skills and the crosswalk data. These are small and IRIS-specific, so they fit the owner's 2026-10-09 ruling: "iris specific tools need to be in litlfred/who-iris".
  • Tool B (redacto) and the medallion pipeline live in their own repository, pinned in index.lock.json like the other layers, or called as a pinned container.
  • The gold output is held by reference, referenced by default. A document's gold graph is materialized only where a scope of interest selected it and the five gates passed.
  • D is optional and later. It serves as a comparison reference in agentic review, after the licence question is answered.

If redacto turns out to be a redaction step rather than an extractor, the recommendation keeps its shape. Redacto becomes a landing → bronze pre-processor, run before Tool B and before the existing ingest-extract-structure on the same bytes, so both tools read the same redacted text and the comparison stays fair. A third "Tool B" extractor then still has to be chosen (section 12, Q1).

5. Consuming the nightly CDN feed

What the feed produces (from scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts and iris-cdn-exporter):

  • a release is a commit in the release-history git repository on Cloudflare Artifacts: BagIt bagit.txt, date-free bag-info.txt, manifest-sha256.txt, tagmanifest-sha256.txt and its detached JWS tagmanifest-sha256.txt.jws (ES256; key from did:web);
  • the payload manifest maps logical paths to SHA-256 digests: records/<handle>.json (the canonical DC record), bitstreams/<handle>/<bundle>/<name>, graph/<partition>, and per-item items/<handle>/manifest-sha256.txt(.jws);
  • bytes are in R2 under sha256/<aa>/<digest>;
  • state/cursor.json is the exporter's own cursor. The new path never moves it.

How the new path consumes it, as process optimus-kg-nightly (section 9):

  1. Start after the exporter's End_Done, as a message start event. A scheduled timer at 04:00 UTC is the fallback. A night with End_NoChange never starts it.
  2. Verify before reading. Resolve the key from the DID document and verify tagmanifest-sha256.txt.jws (the iris-cdn-signing verifier: "Resolves the key from the DID document, never from the package"). An unverified release is refused. That is a state, not an error to retry.
  3. Diff against its own cursor, state/optimus-cursor.json: the release commit and tag-manifest digest it last finished. Use diffManifests from scripts/iris-cdn/bag.ts to get added, changed and removed paths.
  4. Classify each changed handle.
    • Only records/<handle>.json changed (a metadata edit): re-ground the publication node only. Do not re-extract, because the PDF digest did not change (the exporter's "metadata changes and the PDF does not" rule).
    • A bitstream in ORIGINAL changed: a candidate for extraction.
    • removed, or marked withdrawn by the weekly reconciliation: mark the derived nodes and edges withdrawn. Keep them addressable and never delete them, mirroring the reconciliation.
  5. Select by scope. Test each candidate record's DC fields against every active scope of interest (section 8). Out of scope means not processed, and the run report counts it. The gap is the point.
  6. Gate. Check materialize-remote's five gates (size, restrictions, retention, sourceLoss, copyright) for each selected bitstream. restrictions: unknown stays unknown and is never permitted.
  7. Run Tool B over the landing bytes, fetched from R2 by digest and checked against the digest. The work is keyed by bitstream SHA-256 plus Tool B version plus crosswalk version, so an unchanged triple is never re-run. That is the no-churn rule applied to derivations.
  8. bronze → silver → gold, then project the gold output to N-Quads in its own named graph partition, e.g. graph/optimus/<handle>, beside the existing partitions.
  9. Hand off to adjudication (section 7) for every document that also has an L1 KG.
  10. Advance the cursor only when the run completes. Review the run report and open beans for anomalies, as Task_Review in the exporter does.

6. Schema alignment: the crosswalk

Both tools are projected to one comparison form before they are compared:

(subject IRI, predicate IRI, object IRI | literal,
 evidence: { handle, uuid?, section id, page range, quote },
 derivation: derived | inferred | extracted, tool, tool version)

WHO identifiers come first. The publication is always the IRIS item (Handle 10665/…, DSpace UUID, ISBN or govdoc). Entities are grounded to a WHO-owned or WHO-used scheme where one exists. Other schemes link by skos:exactMatch or skos:closeMatch, never by replacing the WHO identifier.

Node types

The DAK component names below are the nine components of a SMART Guidelines Digital Adaptation Kit. The smart-base logical-model names are given as targets to confirm: smart-base is not mounted in this checkout, so they are not verified against its pinned version (section 12, Q6).

OptimusKG-style (Tool B) existing L1 KG (smart-base kg/l1) DAK component / WHO schema target WHO grounding (primary) bridge
— (no publication node) publication DAK L1 source; IRIS DC record Handle, DSpace UUID, ISBN (from records/<handle>.json) dcterms:
— publication-section, publication-element location in L1 section id + page range —
— recommendation Component 2 — Health interventions and recommendations (smart-base recommendation / health-intervention model) the recommendation's own IRI GRADE certainty and strength as properties
Disease (DIS) — (gap: propose condition) Component 2 (condition targeted); Component 5 decision-support logic inputs ICD-11 MMS URI MONDO, UMLS CUI, MeSH
Phenotype (PHE) — (gap: propose finding) Component 5 — Core data elements (observation) ICD-11 signs/symptoms chapter HPO
Drug (DRG) — (gap: propose product) Component 5 data elements (medication); WHO EML ATC code + INN DrugBank, RxNorm
Exposure (EXP) — (gap) Component 5 data elements (risk factor) ICD-11 extension codes where one exists CTD, ExO
Anatomy (ANA) — Component 5 (body site) ICD-11 anatomy extension UBERON
Gene, Pathway, BP/CC/MF — out of scope unless a scope of interest asks — keep referenced
term label / synonym glossary candidate (folio-glossary/v1, SKOS) WHO glossary (glossary/) skos:prefLabel, notation skos:altLabel
— — Components 1 (personas), 3 (user scenarios), 4 (business processes), 6 (indicators), 7 (requirements), 8 (test scenarios) not produced by either tool the L1 editor and DAK authoring

The "gap" rows are a proposal to smart-base: add typed entity nodes to the kg/l1 ontology so a recommendation can be about a condition, product or finding. Until smart-base adopts this, the gold output carries these as its own who-iris types, with skos:closeMatch to the Biolink class. who-iris does not extend smart-base's ontology on its own.

Edges and properties

OptimusKG-style L1 KG / DAK target note
DRG–DIS INDICATION recommendation recommends (intervention for condition), strength and certainty if stated a guideline's recommendation is not a database indication: same pair, different claim. The comparison matches the pair, and the predicate difference is a kind finding, not a conflict
DRG–DIS CONTRAINDICATION recommendation with negative direction ("do not use")
DRG–DIS OFF_LABEL_USE no target WHO guidance seldom states it; record and do not compare
DIS–PHE, DIS–EXP associations Component 5 data-element relations compare only within a scope that asks for them
sources.direct evidence{location, quote} + wasDerivedFrom must resolve to the IRIS handle and a section; an edge without a locator is invalid in gold, the same "no default" rule as catalogue state
evidence_score, evidence_count none in L1 kept as Tool B properties; never mapped to GRADE certainty
relation_assertions, relation_conflict block-qa entries (section 7) intra-tool disagreement is surfaced, not resolved by RELATION_PRIORITY
contains (L1) — structural; Tool B does not produce it. Not compared

The crosswalk itself is data (crosswalk/optimus-l1-dak.json, versioned), not code. Its version is part of the derivation key (section 5, step 7), so a crosswalk change re-projects gold without re-running Tool B.

7. Adjudication between the two tools

This reuses the harness's adjudication and does not invent another.

  • The entry condition is the harness's own (adjudication): mechanical agreement (the comparison script passes), consensus (both tools agree), and adjudicable (the two tools disagree on one claim). A claim only one tool made is not a disagreement. It is a coverage finding, reported but never adjudicated, as the skill says: "A missing entry is not a disagreement."
  • The parties are dispatched untainted (untainted-verification). The adjudicator sees the source passage (the quote and section, read from the library entry) and the two claims anonymised as X and Y, never which tool made which. It uses no tools and says so (tools_used). It never sees either tool's full graph.
  • Rulings are keyed by content, like the translation round-trip (AGENTS.md §Translations). Each ruling is pinned by the hashes of the two claims and the source passage, and stored on a state branch (cat/who-iris/attestations, a new kg-adjudication/ subtree). A re-run that reorders or drops claims needs no re-adjudication.

Agreement metrics (per document, per node/edge type, per night)

metric over why
entity grounding agreement entities both tools found in the same evidence span the same text grounded to different ICD-11 or ATC codes is the commonest real disagreement
pair overlap: Jaccard; precision and recall of each tool with the other as reference (subject, object) pairs after grounding symmetric, and no tool is assumed to be the truth
predicate agreement: Cohen's κ pairs both tools found corrects for chance on a small label set (recommends / contraindicates / associated)
evidence-locator agreement matched claims same section and overlapping pages; a match that cites different passages is suspect
coverage claims only one tool made, by type a tool's blind spots, tracked over time; not adjudicated

Thresholds are not proposed here. They need a baseline over real outputs and are the owner's to set (section 12, Q7).

Outcomes

The caller calls Process_Adjudication and declares its own codes (<cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes="x-right y-right both-wrong both-defensible undecidable"/>).

outcome effect on gold
x-right / y-right the winning claim is promoted to adjudicated; the other is kept and marked rejected with the ruling
both-wrong both kept, marked rejected; a bean opens if it repeats for one tool
both-defensible both kept: the text supports two readings. This is common where a guideline is ambiguous, and it is a finding for the L1 editor
undecidable escalated to the human reviewer lane

Who adjudicates. An untainted agent adjudicates first. Claims of type recommendation, and any claim about a contraindication, always go to a human reviewer (SME or editor), the same lane as ingest-l1-completeness-gate Task_FlagDrift. The agent's ruling is kept beside the human's, never overwritten (human_adjudicated alongside assessed_by). Sampling: every adjudicable recommendation-class claim is ruled on. Other types are sampled with OptimusKG's evaluation plan (stratified by node type, true and false neighbours, sample size from a power analysis), so cost is bounded per night.

8. The L1 editor's scope of interest

The owner wrote "see examples below", but no examples were attached. The examples here are illustrative only and must be replaced with the owner's (section 12, Q8).

What the editor writes

A new document kind, l1-scope-of-interest/v1. It is authored once per L1 document as the first step of the L1 guideline-development process, and it belongs with the L1 document (section 10):

scope: measles-l1                       # one per L1 document
l1Document: <the L1 document's id>
question: >-
  What WHO guidance and evidence governs measles vaccination schedules,
  outbreak response and case management?
pico:
  population: [infants, children under 5, pregnant women]
  intervention: [measles-containing vaccine (MCV1, MCV2), vitamin A]
  comparator: [no vaccination, alternative schedule]
  outcomes: [incidence, mortality, seroconversion, adverse events]
grounding:                              # WHO schemes first
  icd11: ["1F03"]                       # Measles
  mesh: ["Measles", "Measles Vaccine", "Vitamin A"]
  atc: ["J07BD"]                        # measles vaccines
evidenceTypes:                          # what counts as evidence for this L1
  include: [guideline, position paper, systematic review, GRADE evidence profile, technical document]
  exclude: [meeting report, press material, newsletter]
guidelineOfInterest:                    # what makes an item a "guideline of interest"
  - GRC-approved WHO guideline, or WHO position paper published in the WER
  - contains at least one recommendation on the PICO above
  - current: not superseded (dc.relation.isreplacedby, if IRIS fills it)
dates: { from: 2009-01-01 }
languages: [en, fr, es, ar, ru, zh]
regions: [global, AFRO, EMRO, SEARO]    # regional offices' collections
seeds: ["10665/…"]                      # items the editor already knows are in
exclusions: ["10665/…"]

What is generated from it

  1. IRIS DSpace 7 Discovery queries. These use the endpoint and patterns that iris-rest-feed already uses against live IRIS. For example:

    GET /server/api/discover/search/objects?dsoType=ITEM
    &query=(dc.subject.mesh:"Measles Vaccine" OR dc.subject.mesh:"Measles")
           AND dc.date.issued:[2009 TO *]
    &sort=dc.date.accessioned,DESC&page=N&size=100

    Add one query per evidence type on dc.type, and a scope={collectionUuid} query per regional collection. The dc.type values and facet names (f.subject, f.dateIssued, f.itemtype) that IRIS exposes are not verified. The generator must read /server/api/discover/facets first and refuse a field IRIS does not index rather than send a query that silently matches nothing.

  2. OAI-PMH harvest, if IRIS exposes it: verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=oai_dc|qdc&set=<collection set>&from=<date>. IRIS's OAI endpoint is not verified; REST stays the primary route.

  3. A SPARQL query over the who-iris Oxigraph partitions, for items already catalogued (dcterms:subject, dcterms:type, dcterms:issued). It is the same query in the browser and at build time (iris-oxigraph).

  4. The selection predicate that section 5, step 5 applies to each nightly record. It is the same filter run locally over records/<handle>.json, so a new item that matches an active scope is picked up the next night.

  5. Guidance for agentic review of a library KG (who-iris or external). This is a generated checklist that the deep-document-research process (folio-assistant-core) runs, with the scope as the Planner's filter:

    • for each candidate, rule include, exclude or uncertain against the PICO, evidence type and guideline of interest criteria, citing the location (handle + section + page) for every ruling;
    • say what was not found: a PICO element with no evidence is a finding for the editor, not an empty result;
    • for an external library KG (OptimusKG via option D, PubMed, another catalogue), map its records to the comparison form of section 6 first, so the same rulings apply. Never import it to review it; review by reference;
    • the reviewer is untainted with respect to the scope's author. It sees the scope and the candidate, not the editor's expected answer;
    • its rulings feed back as seeds and exclusions, through the editor and never automatically.

A second illustrative scope, kept short: contraceptive use. Its guidelineOfInterest is "WHO Medical eligibility criteria or Selected practice recommendations, any edition, with the edition superseding chain resolved", and its evidence types are [guideline, systematic review]. It shows why a supersession field such as dc.relation.isreplacedby matters; whether IRIS fills that field is not verified.

9. The processes, as the harness expects them

Processes in this repository are BPMN files in processes/. Each activity names its skill (<bootstrap.processes:skill>), with a generated checklist (bun run cat bpmn:checklist) and SVG (bun run cat render:bpmn). The .bpmn files are not drafted in this change. Every activity must name a skill that resolves, and the skills below do not exist yet, so drafting them now would fail check:workflow-refs and the checklist generator. Each process is specified here at the level the BPMN will encode, with activity ids, lanes and skills. Writing the BPMN is the first task of the matching bean.

Lanes used across all three: build-pipeline (the scripts, unattended), optimus-kg-agent (plans, reviews, opens beans; holds no keys), extractor (Tool B, external, pinned), adjudicator (agent, untainted), reviewer (SME/editor, human), l1-editor (human).

optimus-kg-nightly (who-iris)

id lane skill what
Start_AfterExport — — message: the exporter's End_Done; timer fallback
Task_VerifyRelease build-pipeline iris-cdn-signing verify the tag-manifest JWS through did:web; an unverified release ends the run as refused
Task_Diff build-pipeline optimus-kg-feed diff payload manifests since state/optimus-cursor.json
GW_Kind — — metadata-only / bitstream / withdrawn
Task_Reground build-pipeline optimus-kg-feed metadata-only: re-ground the publication node
Task_Withdraw build-pipeline optimus-kg-feed mark derived claims withdrawn, keep them addressable
Task_SelectByScope build-pipeline l1-scope-of-interest apply every active scope's selection predicate
Task_Gates optimus-kg-agent materialize-remote the five gates per bitstream; unknown is not permitted
Call_Extract extractor optimus-kg-extract Tool B: landing → bronze, keyed by (bitstream sha, tool version)
Task_Ground build-pipeline optimus-kg-extract bronze → silver: ground to WHO schemes
Task_Align build-pipeline kg-crosswalk silver → gold through the versioned crosswalk; reject edges without a locator
Call_Partition build-pipeline nquads-distribution project gold to its named-graph partition (platform process, called)
Call_Adjudicate — kg-tool-adjudication the process below, for documents with an L1 KG
Task_AdvanceCursor build-pipeline optimus-kg-feed only after a complete run
Task_Review optimus-kg-agent optimus-kg-feed run report; beans for anomalies (yield far from median, adjudication rate jump, gate unknown spike)

kg-tool-adjudication (folio-assistant-core; generic over any two extractors)

id lane skill what
Task_Project build-pipeline kg-crosswalk both outputs → comparison form

12. Open questions for the owner

  1. What is redacto? The repository, package or URL, and whether it is an extractor or a redaction step. If it redacts, which tool extracts?
  2. What does "adapt OptimusKG" mean here? Its architecture, schema and provenance model (what section 3 assumes), or also its data, as an external library KG (option D)?
  3. Where may Python/Kedro run? In a new repository under litlfred (option C, recommended), or tolerated inside who-iris (option A)?
  4. Volume. Should the nightly path process only items selected by an active scope (recommended, because the gap is the point), or every new IRIS item?
  5. Licences. OptimusKG's data keeps each source's licence, some of them academic or non-commercial only. May WHO use it for comparison? Who answers the copyright gate for IRIS bitstreams fed to an external tool?
  6. DAK targets. Which smart-base version and logical models are the alignment targets? Should the typed entity nodes (condition, product, finding) be proposed to smart-base's kg/l1 ontology?
  7. Adjudication policy. Who sits in the human reviewer lane, and is "every recommendation-class disagreement goes to a human" right? The metric thresholds should wait for a baseline (bean 9).
  8. The examples. The request said "see examples below", but none were attached. Please send the scope-of-interest examples you had in mind; the measles and contraception scopes in section 8 are placeholders.
  9. Network. optimuskg.ai and arxiv.org are blocked from these sessions (pypi.org is reachable). To quote the paper's evaluation figures, allow them in the environment's network settings or attach the PDF.
